name: Projective blocking sets with small line intersections in PG(2,7)
description: construct() -> distinct point indices in 0..56 for PG(2,7). Point order is (1,x,y) lexicographically for x,y=0..6, then (0,1,x), then (0,0,1). Every projective line must meet the set. Minimize the maximum intersection with any line; line-contained sets are allowed but score at least 8. The local task searches all point subsets in the prime plane of order seven; it does not constrain candidates to unions of algebraic curves or reproduce that paper's proof. The optimum is 4: an exhaustive search shows that no blocking set meets every line in at most 3 points, so this is a rediscovery task.

limitations: Solved finite case: No blocking set of PG(2,7) meets every line in at most 3 points, while one meeting every line in at most 4 points exists.
A result in this one Desarguesian plane says nothing about a uniform constant across arbitrary finite planes. The seed is a full line and is explicitly a trivial blocking set.
Independent Python implementation; no paper text, upstream evaluator, Lean proof or prize-bank content is redistributed. Candidate Python executes as trusted research code.

state_of_the_art.statement: No blocking set of PG(2,7) meets every line in at most 3 points, while one meeting every line in at most 4 points exists. An exhaustive branch-and-bound search (scripts/check_state_of_the_art.py) establishes both, so the optimum is 4. The uniform question over all projective planes is Erdős Problem #1159.
